title: Solomon Anointed King
summary: As David ages, his son Adonijah declares himself king with Joab and Abiathar's support, but Nathan and Bathsheba persuade David to make Solomon king instead, and Solomon is anointed at Gihon while Adonijah flees to the altar.

title: David's Death and Solomon's Purge
summary: David charges Solomon to walk faithfully with God and deal with old scores before he dies; Solomon then executes Adonijah and Joab, exiles Abiathar, and later executes Shimei, securing his throne.

title: Solomon Asks for Wisdom
summary: Solomon marries Pharaoh's daughter and, when God offers him anything he wants in a dream at Gibeon, asks for wisdom to govern rather than wealth; he then proves that wisdom by rightly judging between two women over a living child.

title: Solomon's Officials and Renowned Wisdom
summary: Solomon organizes his kingdom under a council of officials and twelve district governors who supply the royal household in turn, and his wisdom, three thousand proverbs, and over a thousand songs make him famous beyond every neighboring nation.

title: Solomon's Covenant with Hiram of Tyre
summary: Solomon asks King Hiram of Tyre for cedar and cypress timber to build the temple, and Hiram supplies it in exchange for grain and oil while Solomon raises a massive labor force of conscripted workers and stonecutters.

title: Building the Temple
summary: In his fourth year as king, Solomon begins building the temple with cedar-paneled walls and a gold-covered inner sanctuary carved with cherubim and palm trees, and the LORD promises to dwell among Israel if Solomon obeys his commands.

title: Solomon's Palace and the Temple's Bronze Furnishings
summary: Solomon spends thirteen years building his own palace, then has the bronze craftsman Hiram cast the temple's two great pillars, the bronze basin called the sea on twelve oxen, and its stands, basins, and other furnishings.

title: The Temple Dedication
summary: Solomon brings the ark into the finished temple, where the LORD's glory fills it as a cloud; he dedicates it with a prayer asking God to hear prayer offered toward it, then the people sacrifice thousands of offerings and feast for seven days.

title: The LORD's Second Warning to Solomon
summary: The LORD appears to Solomon a second time, warning that disobedience will bring exile and the temple's destruction; Solomon gives Hiram twenty cities as payment, conscripts forced labor for his building projects, and sends a fleet from Ezion-geber to Ophir for gold.

title: The Queen of Sheba Visits Solomon
summary: The queen of Sheba travels to Jerusalem to test Solomon with hard questions and is overwhelmed by his wisdom and wealth, giving him gold and spices before returning home; the chapter closes by cataloging Solomon's gold, throne, and trading fleets.

title: Solomon's Foreign Wives and Decline
summary: Solomon's many foreign wives turn his heart to other gods, so the LORD announces he will tear away the kingdom and raises up adversaries, including Jeroboam, whom the prophet Ahijah promises ten tribes; Solomon dies after forty years as king.

title: The Kingdom Divides
summary: Rehoboam rejects the elders' gentle advice for the young men's harsh answer, and Israel rebels against the house of David, making Jeroboam king over the north; Jeroboam then sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan so his people won't worship in Jerusalem.

title: The Man of God and the Lion
summary: A man of God from Judah confronts Jeroboam's altar at Bethel and it splits as a sign, but an old prophet later tricks him into eating there against the LORD's command, and a lion kills him on the road as judgment.
blurb: A lion kills the disobedient prophet

title: Judgment on Jeroboam and Rehoboam
summary: The prophet Ahijah recognizes Jeroboam's disguised wife and pronounces doom on his house; their son dies as she returns home, and Jeroboam soon dies too, while in Judah, Egypt's king Shishak plunders the temple during Rehoboam's reign.

title: Abijam and Asa of Judah
summary: Abijam reigns briefly and sinfully over Judah, but his son Asa removes his grandmother Maacah for her idol and reforms the kingdom, while in Israel, Nadab is assassinated and Baasha wipes out Jeroboam's entire house to fulfill prophecy.
blurb: Asa's reforms; Baasha ends Jeroboam's line

title: Zimri, Omri, and Ahab
summary: Zimri assassinates Elah, reigns only seven days, and burns the palace down around himself when the army makes Omri king; Omri builds Samaria as Israel's capital, and his son Ahab marries Jezebel and builds an altar to Baal, becoming Israel's worst king yet.

title: Elijah, the Ravens, and the Widow
summary: Elijah announces a drought to Ahab and is fed by ravens at the brook Cherith; when it dries up he goes to Zarephath, where a widow's flour and oil never run out during the famine, and he later revives her dead son.
blurb: The widow of Zarephath's flour and oil

title: Elijah on Mount Carmel
summary: Elijah confronts Ahab and challenges the prophets of Baal to a contest on Mount Carmel; when only his soaked sacrifice is consumed by fire, the people declare the LORD is God, the false prophets are killed, and Elijah's prayer ends the drought with rain.

title: Elijah at Horeb
summary: Fleeing Jezebel's threat, Elijah asks God to let him die, but an angel feeds him for a journey to Horeb, where the LORD speaks not in wind, earthquake, or fire but in a low whisper, and sends him to anoint successors and call Elisha.
blurb: The LORD speaks in a whisper

title: Ahab Defeats Ben-hadad Twice
summary: Syria's king Ben-hadad besieges Samaria and is defeated twice by Ahab with prophetic help, but when Ahab spares Ben-hadad's life instead of killing him, an unnamed prophet condemns him for releasing a man the LORD had devoted to destruction.
blurb: Ahab spares Ben-hadad; a prophet's rebuke

title: Naboth's Vineyard
summary: Ahab sulks when Naboth refuses to sell his family's vineyard, so Jezebel arranges false witnesses to have Naboth stoned to death; Elijah confronts Ahab with the LORD's judgment on his house, and Ahab humbles himself in mourning.
blurb: Jezebel frames Naboth for his vineyard

title: Micaiah's Prophecy and Ahab's Death
summary: Ahab and Jehoshaphat plan to retake Ramoth-gilead; four hundred prophets promise victory, but Micaiah alone truthfully predicts defeat and is imprisoned for it, and Ahab dies in battle from a stray arrow just as Micaiah foretold.
